notes: Parts are the same as step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.
The 100 ohm series resistor (r2) is used as the parts list and text say. The schematic labels it 10K.

Speaker: pin 9 goes through r2 to speaker lead 1, and speaker lead 2 goes to ground. In the image the speaker's red lead goes into the breadboard at column 9, in the same strip as r2's top leg. Its black lead runs to the GND pin beside AREF. I modelled that black lead as wire5, twisted to speaker lead 2 and ending on GND.3.

Breadboard rows follow the image's lettering. The image's top half (rows f-j) is written as bank 'b' and its bottom half (rows a-e) as bank 't'. The image is flipped relative to the catalogue's description, so the labels are consistent but only the strips matter.

Column mapping: r2 sits in column 9 and bridges the centre gap (9b.f to 9t.e). The photoresistor sits in column 21 and also bridges the gap (21b.f to 21t.e). The 5V wire lands at 21b.h, in the strip of the photoresistor's top leg. The A0 wire lands at 21t.d, in the strip of the photoresistor's bottom leg and r1's left leg. r1 runs from 21t.c to 24t.c. The ground wire lands at 24t.b.
GND.1 and GND.3 are used for the two ground connections. The Uno joins its GND pins internally, so the choice only matters for naming.
